# 4.2.1 Categorical and Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility

This section from the FoodShare Wisconsin Policy Handbook (Release 26-02, August 12, 2026) covers eligibility pathways based on categorical status.

## Categorical Eligibility Overview

The policy defines a categorical food unit as one where adult members receive: "SSI, TANF benefits, [or] GA (general assistance) benefits." These units face no gross, net, or asset testing requirements, with limited exceptions for smaller households.

## Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE)

Most food units qualify under BBCE when gross monthly income stays at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) and members receive access to Job Center of Wisconsin services through TANF funding. These households also have no asset test requirements.

## Loss of BBCE Status

Food units lose broad-based categorical eligibility through several circumstances: exceeding 200% FPL income limits, member disqualification for Intentional Program Violation sanctions, drug felony convictions, failure to comply with work rules, or receipt of substantial lottery winnings.

## Transitional FoodShare and EBD Cases

Transitional FoodShare recipients lose categorical eligibility during their five-month certification period. Elderly, Blind, or Disabled households exceeding 200% FPL must meet regular SNAP standards: no gross income ceiling, 100% FPL net limit, and specific asset restrictions.

# FoodShare Wisconsin Policy - Version 22-03

**Release Date:** 12/05/2022 | **Effective Date:** 10/01/2022

## Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE)

"Most food units are considered broad-based categorically eligible if their gross income is at or below 200% FPL and the language describing 'Job Center of Wisconsin' services..." is issued on the notice of decision.

## 200% FPL Income Test

Food units lose BBCE eligibility if "Total gross income is above 200%" FPL. Additionally, when verified gross income exceeds this threshold, "the case will close" with a notice citing excess income.

## One- or Two-Person Minimum Allotment Exception

"Except during an initial month, all eligible one- and two-person food units shall receive the minimum $23 allotment when the gross income is below 200% FPL and the net adjusted income exceeds the net income limit."

## Elderly, Blind, or Disabled (EBD) Food Units Over 200% FPL

EBD food units with gross income exceeding 200% FPL must be evaluated under regular SNAP rules, which impose "no gross income limit" but require "net income that does not exceed 100% FPL" and assets not exceeding $4,250.

# SNAP Benefit Calculations for Small Households

## Minimum Allotments (One- and Two-Person Households)

According to the regulation, except during initial months: "all eligible one-person and two-person households shall receive minimum monthly allotments equal to the minimum benefit."

The minimum benefit is defined as "8 percent of the maximum allotment for a household of one, rounded to the nearest whole dollar."

## Zero-Benefit Households (Three or More Members)

When a household with three or more members computes to zero benefits, state agencies have two options:

**Option A - Denial:** "The State agency shall deny the household's application on the grounds that its net income exceeds the level at which benefits are issued."

**Option B - Suspension:** Alternatively, "The State agency shall certify the household but suspend its participation" subject to specific conditions regarding notification, change reporting, and conversion procedures if circumstances change.

These provisions ensure that very small households receive at least minimal assistance, while larger households with zero computed benefits receive clear guidance on their eligibility status and options for future participation.
